Unlimited 2% cash rewards -- Cardholders earn an unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, with no categories to activate or earnings limits to track.

And they often are also subject to a cap and limited in what purchases they apply to. The Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is perfect for someone that wants an easy-to-use card that still offers high rewards: you’ll earn a best-in-class flat rewards right away on your purchases -- with no limits or hoops to jump through.

$200 cash rewards welcome offer -- New Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card holders can earn a $200 cash rewards welcome offer for spending just $500 in purchases in the first 3 months. Not only is this a very competitive sign-up bonus for a card with no annual fee, but it's also one of the things that sets this Wells Fargo credit card apart from other 2% back cards. 12 months from account opening 0% APR intro offer -- New cardholders can enjoy 0% intro APR on both new purchases and qualifying balance transfers for a full 12 months from account opening. No annual fee -- In many cases, high rewards rates mean high annual fees. Not with the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which sports a $0 annual fee.

Who should get the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card
The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is best for people carrying high-interest debt or planning a large purchase they want to spread out over time.
You get nearly two years of breathing room with no interest, which can save a lot of money while you pay things off.

If you're looking for cash back or travel rewards, this is not the card for you. The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card has no rewards program and no welcome bonus. It loses most of its value the moment the intro period ends.
What I like about the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card
Long 0% intro APR period

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card's headline feature is 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. (A 17.49%, 23.99%, or 28.24% Variable APR applies after.)
That's one of the longest 0% APR periods you'll find anywhere -- which is why it earned Motley Fool Money's award for Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2026.
This long intro APR is particularly handy for large balances (think anything $5,000+). The longer the promo window, the less you need to pay each month to clear your balance while paying no interest.
$0 annual fee

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card charges no annual fee, so it costs nothing to keep in your wallet. For anyone building credit history -- or, like me, holding onto a top credit card for the long haul -- that's a real plus.
Keeping the card open can help your credit score by lengthening your average credit history over time.
Cellphone protection

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card includes cellphone protection when you pay your monthly phone bill with the card. It covers up to $600 per claim for theft or damage, with a $25 deductible, and you can file up to two claims per 12-month period.
I've never had to use cellphone insurance, but as a frequent phone-dropper and generally clumsy person, I've always loved having it in my back pocket.
Credit card comparison
We recommend comparing options to ensure the card you're selecting is the best fit for you. To make your search easier, here's a short list of standout credit cards.
Downsides to consider
No ongoing rewards
The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card earns no rewards. If you want a card with long-term perks like cash back or travel points, this isn't it.

A strong alternative is the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card (rates and fees), which earns a flat 2% cash rewards on purchases for a $0 annual fee. It's our Best Overall Credit Card of 2026, and a fan favorite for flat-rate rewards.
High balance transfer fee
The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card charges a balance transfer fee of 5%, min: $5 -- this is on the high side for a balance transfer card.
If you move a $10,000 balance, you'd owe a $500 fee, even though you'd pay the balance off at 0% during the intro period.

Run the math before you transfer, because the fee should cost less than the interest you'd otherwise pay. If you won't clear the balance within the 0% APR period, then an alternative balance transfer card with a lower transfer fee may serve you better.
Foreign transaction fees

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card charges a 3% foreign transaction fee, so you'll pay extra on purchases made outside the U.S. If you travel abroad and want to skip that cost, consider one of our favorite travel credit cards.
It also has no purchase protection or extended warranty on purchases.
What credit score do you need for the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card?

You'll generally need good to excellent credit (Motley Fool Money estimates this to be a FICO® Score of about 670 or higher) to qualify for the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card. Wells Fargo doesn't publish an official cutoff, and applicants closer to 700 tend to be the best-qualified candidates.

Keep in mind, your score isn't the only factor. Wells Fargo also weighs your income, existing debt, and overall credit history. You can check for pre-selected offers on Wells Fargo's site without a hard inquiry to gauge your chances first.
What credit limit can you get with the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card?

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card comes with a minimum credit limit of $1,000, and higher scores and income generally earn higher limits. Wells Fargo sets your limit individually based on your full credit profile, so two applicants can get very different lines of credit.

Your starting limit isn't permanent, though. Once your account is open and in good standing, usually after six to 12 months, you can request an increase. Or, Wells Fargo may raise it automatically for on-time payments and low utilization.
How to do a balance transfer with the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card

To get the 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on qualifying balance transfers (then 17.49%, 23.99%, or 28.24% Variable APR), you must complete qualifying transfers within 120 days of opening your account.
I recommend starting the transfer online or by phone as soon as you're approved. Having your old account details ready speeds things up.
One important note: you can't transfer a balance from another Wells Fargo or affiliated card. Transfers have to come from a different issuer, and the 5%, min: $5 transfer fee applies to each one.
How to apply for the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card
Applying for the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is quick. Here's what to do:

items: Start the application right here from this page.
Provide your personal and financial details -- name, income, address, and Social Security number.
Review the terms and conditions, then submit your application.
Wait for a decision, and start using your card once approved.

blocks.text: Approvals are usually instant, but can take a few days if Wells Fargo needs to verify some of your information.
Is the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card worth it?
Yes, the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is worth it if your priority is paying off debt or financing a large purchase without interest. Very few cards give you a long no-interest runway like this.
It's not worth it if you want rewards or perks after the intro period, since it offers neither.
Ready to make a dent in your debt? Apply for the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card today -- awarded Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2026.

articles.title: Red rainfall warning up over Zambales, Bataan; NCR under yellow alert
articles.summary: Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.

blocks.text: Motorists and pedestrians are drenched during a heavy downpour in Quezon City as the habagat continues to batter in Metro Manila and neighboring provinces with strong winds and heavy rainfall on Aug. 8, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.
In its heavy rainfall advisory issued at 11 a.m., state weather bureau PAGASA said that serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas under the red warning level.
The following areas are under the red warning level:

items: Zambales
Bataan: Morong, Hermosa and Dinalupihan

blocks.text: PAGASA said flooding is still threatening in areas under the orange warning level, which covers:

items: Pampanga
Tarlac
Bulacan

articles.title: It works! Lucena inventor creates trash-collecting robot from recycled materials
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city. The device…

blocks.text: (Photo by Isagani Inciong via Danny Estacio)
LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city.
The device was constructed using old plastic containers, aluminum, and galvanized wire mesh.
It is equipped with a garbage lifter designed to easily gather and collect floating debris.
The robot is operated via a remote control—similar to those used in computer games—that controls a small motor attached to the unit.
According to Isagani Inciong, an electronics technician and the device's inventor, he conceived the project to help reduce floating river debris, particularly plastic waste.
Tests conducted at the Iyam River proved the robot effective at gathering and retrieving floating trash.
Inciong added that aside from being fun to operate, the robot offers significant environmental benefits.
He believes that if more people use or "play" with this type of robot, a larger volume of waste can be recovered from waterways.

He also called on local government units (LGUs) to take notice of his invention and expressed willingness to collaborate with authorities to refine the design and build a larger version of the robot to support more extensive river rehabilitation efforts.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Misamis Oriental family deaths in 2021 due to COVID-19, not vaccines
articles.summary: A viral Facebook reel recycles a report from a 2021 incident involving four family members in Misamis Oriental; the health department has clarified that the deaths were associated with COVID-19…

blocks.text: Claim: Four members of one family in Laguindingan, Misamis Oriental, died because of COVID-19 vaccines after receiving their jabs.

Why we fact-checked this: A widely shared Facebook reel claims that four members of the same family died because of COVID-19 vaccines. Posted on August 16, 2026, it garnered around 19,400 reactions, 1,700 comments, and 19,000 shares as of writing.
The reel was posted by the Facebook account Unsa Gyod Gisulti SaBibliya, which has around 60,000 followers.
The account’s biography shows an anti-vaccination position, stating: “Va666ines= Mark Of The Beast! ✓Mandated (Rev13:16) ✓Required (Rev13:17) ✓Deceit (Rev18:23,19:20).”
It also has multiple reels opposing vaccines, many of which use the phrase, “Va666$in TATAK666 ng Antikristo nililinlang at nilalason mga kabataan.”
(Vaccines are marks of the Antichrist, deceiving and poisoning the youth.)

The post presents the incident, using a news report from GMA Regional TV, as evidence that COVID-19 vaccines were responsible for the deaths and questions the Department of Health (DOH)’s explanation of the case.
The facts: The four deaths were real, occurring between August 1 and 8, 2021, but available evidence does not support the claim that COVID-19 vaccination caused them.
According to an August 21, 2021 report by the Philippine News Agency, the DOH Region 10 found that the four individuals showed COVID-19 symptoms.
About 10 family members and neighbors were also infected. Investigators identified possible exposure at a wake in Barangay Patag, Cagayan de Oro City, and at a family birthday gathering.
Jasper Kent Ola, the nurse-epidemiologist who supervised the investigation, explained that the deaths occurred successively because of the different infection and incubation periods of the virus.
The Philippine Information Agency (PIA) later reported on August 23, 2021 that the four deceased family members tested positive for COVID-19 through RT-PCR tests.

The DOH-10 Regional Adverse Effect Following Immunization Committee also conducted a causality assessment based on case-tracking reports and found that the cases were “inconsistent with causal association to immunization.”
Investigators concluded that the individuals were likely already incubating the virus around the time of immunization.

Vaccination in the Philippines: The Facebook reel surfaced amid the DOH’s rollout of its nationwide Measles-Rubella Supplementary Immunization Activity this month. In an August 27 PIA report, the DOH said false information about vaccines continues to circulate on social media and may discourage parents from having their children immunized.
To counter this, the health department is partnering with local government units to conduct health education sessions and share reliable information on vaccines through social media.
Earlier, Rappler debunked circulating posts casting doubt on the safety of the measles-rubella vaccines. – Ahyenne Neleah Estacio/Rappler.com

Ahyenne Neleah Estacio is a graduating Bachelor of Arts in Communication student and campus journalist at Holy Angel University. The current senior editor and former editor-in-chief of The Angelite, she is an Aries Rufo Fellow for 2026.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: No place for violence, bullying in Baguio - Mayor Magalong
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City. This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City.
This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he assured that the two separate violent incidents involving high school students are now being handled by the Baguio City Police Office.
Magalong urged the public not to circulate a video involving one of the cases to prevent online abuse.
"While we do not condone these acts among the youth, we should also respect the dignity, privacy, and well-being of the children involved."

He asked the public not to "share, repost, or further circulate the video" as further dissemination could expose minors to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse.
Magalong urged the public to allow police authorities, school officials, and social workers to address the two separate cases judiciously.
“Let us not amplify violence. Let us protect our children and help build a safer, kinder, and more respectful Baguio,” he said.
The police said the two cases are being handled separately with details treated confidentially because minors are involved.
The first incident involving students reportedly occurred outside the school premises of a high school at around 3 p.m. on August 26.
Investigation report said complaints were filed with Police Station 2 and the minors involved, described as Grade 9 and Grade 10 students, have been identified.
Personnel of the Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) coordinated with the school authorities while appropriate intervention was undertaken with the assistance of social workers.
Police Station 2 had scheduled another coordination meeting on August 28 to discuss the matter and the appropriate interventions.
The second incident reportedly involved Grade 7 and Grade 9 students from another secondary school and was reported to Police Station 5 at around 1 p.m. on August 27.
The incident allegedly happened during recess on August 24 inside a classroom causing an injury to the complainant.

Police said WCPD personnel coordinated with the school principal and class advisers and a dialogue was later held with the students and their parents or guardians with administrative sanctions expected to be imposed.

articles.title: DSWD, DDB pilot program to curb drug abuse risks among street children, out-of-school youth
articles.summary: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and…

blocks.text: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and psychosocial support.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), in partnership with the Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB), is piloting “Program Silong,” an integrated program to be implemented through Special Drug Education Centers (SDECs).
The agencies conducted a week-long training for the program’s pilot implementation from Aug. 24 to 28 in Quezon City.
DSWD Special Assistant to the Secretary for Innovations Helen Suzara said the initiative seeks to strengthen drug and substance abuse prevention efforts among children and young people.
“Silong is an important step in strengthening our collective efforts towards drug abuse prevention, particularly among children and the young people,” Suzara said during the opening of the training.
The program has four components covering drug abuse prevention education, family involvement and support, community mobilization, and psychosocial and auxiliary services.
The education component includes toolkits designed for children, early to late adolescents, and parents or caregivers.

The family component will provide interventions to help parents and caregivers support drug abuse prevention efforts, while the community component will encourage communities to develop and implement prevention activities.
The psychosocial component will use pre- and post-assessments to identify the needs of children in street situations and out-of-school youth and monitor their progress.
Suzara described Program Silong as “a pioneering initiative, the first of its kind in the Philippines and in the ASEAN region.”
The program will initially be piloted in Muntinlupa City, Occidental Mindoro, and Zamboanga del Sur.

DSWD said the initiative is in line with its mandate under the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, to provide drug abuse prevention and developmental services to vulnerable children and youth.
It will also involve community volunteers and local government implementers in carrying out prevention activities in the pilot areas.

articles.summary: NUEVA ERA, Ilocos Norte — A 24-year-old college student was killed while his girlfriend was wounded when they were shot by a motorcycle-riding gunman in front of their residence in Barangay Uguis…

blocks.text: NUEVA ERA, Ilocos Norte — A 24-year-old college student was killed while his girlfriend was wounded when they were shot by a motorcycle-riding gunman in front of their residence in Barangay Uguis here Thursday night, August 27.
Police identified the fatality as alias "Jay,” a resident of Sitio Tres, Barangay Uguis.
His girlfriend, also a college student, and a resident of Burgos, Ilocos Norte, suffered gunshot wounds in the leg and abdomen.

Police said the victims had just arrived home at around 7:30 p.m. when a 19-year-old suspect, a resident of the same barangay, allegedly approached them on a motorcycle and fired four shots from a still unknown firearm
Jay sustained multiple gunshot wounds. He and his girlfriend were rushed to a hospital in Sinait, Ilocos Sur, but he was declared dead upon arrival.
The suspect is now the subject of a hot-pursuit operation.
The Nueva Era police are continuing their investigation and awaiting the SOCO findings.

articles.title: School bag yields marijuana, 8 live bullets; student arrested in Tuguegarao
articles.summary: TUGUEGARAO CITY — A routine security check at a private school here led to the arrest of a 20-year-old college student after suspected marijuana and eight live 9mm rounds were allegedly found in his…

blocks.text: TUGUEGARAO CITY — A routine security check at a private school here led to the arrest of a 20-year-old college student after suspected marijuana and eight live 9mm rounds were allegedly found in his backpack on Monday, August 24.

Police said the student, identified only as alias “Mar,” a resident of Barangay Ngarag, Cabagan, Isabela, was stopped for inspection at about 11:56 a.m. at the school’s pedestrian entrance along Balzain Highway in Barangay Centro 12.
A female security officer conducting the routine bag inspection reportedly discovered two pieces of suspected marijuana weighing 1.78 grams and valued at about P213.
A glass tube reportedly containing marijuana residue and eight live 9mm ammunition were also found inside the backpack.
The discovery prompted the security officer to alert authorities, resulting in the student’s arrest and turnover to the Tuguegarao City Police Station.
Police said the confiscated items would be turned over to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 2 for examination and proper disposition.
The student is facing charges under Sections 11 and 12 of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, for alleged possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia.
He is also facing a charge under Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Law on Firearms and Ammunition, for alleged illegal possession of the eight live rounds.
Authorities are continuing their investigation into the source and intended use of the ammunition and suspected illegal drugs.

articles.title: No more delayed PDL release: Remulla justifies proposed transfer of BJMP to DOJ
articles.summary: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) ought to be transferred to the Department of Justice (DOJ), if only to avoid delays in the release of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) due to messy…

blocks.text: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) ought to be transferred to the Department of Justice (DOJ), if only to avoid delays in the release of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) due to messy paperwork.
Thus, said DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla during the agency’s marathon budget hearing before the House Committee on Appropriations Thursday, Aug. 27.
It was Makabayan lawmaker ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio who raised the unfortunate issue of inmates being kept in BJMP custody because of the clerical matter.
Remulla responded by saying that it would be better to transfer the BJMP to the DOJ since the latter handles the records of PDLs.
“It is our position that the BJMP should be transferred under the [DOJ], under the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor),” he told Tinio, a deputy minority leader.
“Dalawang pong karpeta eh, may karpeta ang BJMP, may karpeta ang Bucor," noted the DILG chief (There are two folders, the BJMP has its own folder, and the BuCor has its own folder).
"I think it would be prudent for Congress to help us into combining the BuCor and BJMP into one facility since they perform the same jobs, basically, they just mirroring each other,” he reckoned.
Aside from the BJMP, Remulla also proposed transferring to the DOJ municipal and provincial jails.

“So we’re asking Congress for help, the President’s help, in combining the two agencies for more efficient use of resources and for fair treatment of the Persons Deprived of Liberty if they have to release of not,” Remulla said.

Under the present system, inmates or PDLs are detained in municipal, city, and provincial jails while their cases are being heard. Once sentenced, they are transferred to the New Bilibid Prison (NBP), which is managed by the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) under the DOJ.
Located in Muntinlupa City, the NBP has a population of over 20,000, which is nearly 200 percent above its intended capacity.

articles.summary: Police arrested a 41-year-old man for allegedly stealing a car radiator worth P3,500 from the vehicle of a police officer in Barangay Maharlika, Quezon City, on Wednesday, Aug. 26. The suspect,…

blocks.text: Police recovered the car radiator allegedly stolen from a police officer's vehicle in Quezon City. (Photo courtesy of QCPD)
Police arrested a 41-year-old man for allegedly stealing a car radiator worth P3,500 from the vehicle of a police officer in Barangay Maharlika, Quezon City, on Wednesday, Aug. 26.
The suspect, identified only as alias “JM,” allegedly took the radiator from a vehicle parked outside an automotive service establishment on Mayon Street at around 9:20 p.m.
Police said the victim, a police officer, had brought his vehicle to the establishment for repair due to a defective radiator.
While the vehicle was being serviced, the victim temporarily placed the radiator on the cemented pavement outside the establishment before briefly going inside.
When he returned, he discovered that the radiator was missing.
The victim immediately sought assistance from personnel of the La Loma Police Station (PS 1), who were conducting patrol operations in the area.
The responding officers and the victim conducted a roving search in the vicinity, which led to the arrest of the suspect and recovery of the stolen radiator from his possession.

Police records showed that the suspect had a previous case for an alleged violation of Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, in June 2024, and cases involving Presidential Decree No. 1602 (illegal gambling), Republic Act No. 10591 (firearms law), and City Ordinance No. 5121 (anti-deadly weapons measure) in April 2018.
The suspect is facing a theft charge before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office.

articles.title: Ilocos region logs 6 deaths due to leptospirosis
articles.summary: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — Six people have died from leptospirosis in the Ilocos Region since January, prompting the Department of Health (DOH) to warn residents against unnecessary contact with…

blocks.text: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — Six people have died from leptospirosis in the Ilocos Region since January, prompting the Department of Health (DOH) to warn residents against unnecessary contact with floodwaters amid continued rains.

The Regional Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit recorded 85 leptospirosis cases and six deaths from January 1 to August 8, 2026, with Pangasinan accounting for the most cases at 46, followed by La Union with 13, Ilocos Norte with 12, and Ilocos Sur and Dagupan City with six each.
Although the figure is 52 percent lower than the 177 cases recorded during the same period last year, the DOH said the deaths highlight the continuing danger posed by floodwater exposure.
“Floodwater exposure is not without risk, especially when there are wounds or breaks in the skin,” said Dr. Rheuel C. Bobis, head of the Regional Communicable Disease Cluster.

Leptospirosis is a potentially fatal bacterial infection caused by exposure to water or soil contaminated by the urine of infected animals, particularly rats. The bacteria can enter the body through cuts or wounds.

The DOH advised residents to avoid wading through floodwaters whenever possible. Those who cannot avoid exposure should wear waterproof boots, cover their wounds, and immediately wash exposed areas with soap and clean water.
Residents should seek medical attention if they develop fever, headache, muscle or calf pain, vomiting, chills, abdominal pain, red eyes, or yellowing of the skin or eyes after flood water exposure.
Bobis also warned against taking antibiotics such as doxycycline without medical advice, stressing that the need for preventive medication depends on the type and extent of exposure.
“Doxycycline is a prescription medicine,” he said, urging residents to consult the nearest health center for proper assessment.

articles.title: Alcaraz opens US Open title defense against Safiullin; Venus draws Kenin
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Carlos Alcaraz will open the defense of his U.S. Open title against an opponent who made a strong run at Wimbledon while the Spaniard was sidelined with an injury. Along with some…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Carlos Alcaraz will open the defense of his U.S. Open title against an opponent who made a strong run at Wimbledon while the Spaniard was sidelined with an injury.

Along with some interesting opening-round matches, the draws for men's and women's singles Thursday, Aug. 27, delivered one what-could-have-been possibility: Had Serena Williams decided to play, there could have been a Williams sisters showdown in Round 1.

When Venus Williams was given a wild card into the event at 46, the U.S. Tennis Association initially held one spot, which surely would have gone to Serena if the six-time U.S. Open champion wanted to play after returning to tennis for the first time since 2022. When the 44-year-old decided to only compete in doubles, the USTA awarded that last wild card over the weekend to American Sofia Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion.
On Thursday, Venus Williams and Kenin were randomly drawn to face each other.
Main draw play at the final Grand Slam tournament of the season begins Sunday.

Alcaraz is the No. 2 seed and will face Roman Safiullin. It will be Alcaraz's first singles match since April, after the two-time U.S. Open champion was forced to miss the French Open and Wimbledon because of a right wrist injury.

The Spaniard returned to play with Serena Williams in the mixed doubles tournament and looked rusty. He may have to be sharper against Safiullin, who reached the fourth round at Wimbledon, upsetting Andrey Rublev and Joao Fonseca along the way before falling to 24-time Grand Slam singles champion Novak Djokovic in four sets.
Safiullin also upset Alcaraz, ranked No. 2 at the time, in the ATP Masters 1000 in Paris in 2023. Alcaraz avenged that loss the following year at the Paris Olympics in their lone other meeting.
Alexander Zverev, the French Open champion who became the No. 1 seed in New York when Jannik Sinner pulled out with a knee injury, will open against Italian Lorenzo Sonego.

Two-time defending women's champion Aryna Sabalenka opens against Camila Osorio. The top-ranked Sabalenka, who has struggled during the North American hard-court season, could face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the No. 6 seed, in the quarterfinals.

The other potential women's quarterfinals: No. 2 Elena Rybakina vs. No. 8 Iga Swiatek, and No. 4 Coco Gauff vs. No. 5 Mirra Andreeva, the French Open champion, in the bottom half; and No. 3 Jessica Pegula vs. No. 7 Karolina Muchova in Sabalenka's half.
Pegula, who opens against Elena-Gabriela Ruse, would play the Williams-Kenin winner in the second round.

The potential men's quarters: No. 1 Zverev vs. No. 6 Alex de Minaur, and No. 3 Felix Auger-Aliassime vs. No. 5 Flavio Cobolli in the top half; and No. 2 Alcaraz vs. No. 8 Ben Shelton, and No. 4 Djokovic vs. No. 7 Daniil Medvedev in the bottom half.
No. 10 seed Arthur Fils, coming off the title in the Cincinnati Open, faces two-time Grand Slam finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas, who was once ranked No. 3, in the first round.

Stan Wawrinka, the 2016 U.S. Open champion who received a wild card to play in his final Grand Slam tournament before retiring, faces Matteo Berrettini, the 2021 Wimbledon runner-up, to open a second straight major tournament. Berrettini won in four sets — all tiebreakers — at the All England Club. The winner would likely face Djokovic in the second round.

Rublev, the No. 23 seed, faces 2014 U.S. Open champion Marin Cilic. No. 13 Lorenzo Musetti, who reached the quarterfinals in New York last year, opens against Britain's Arthur Fery, who lost to Zverev in the Wimbledon semifinals.

Some first-round matches won't be determined until the conclusion of the qualifying tournaments, which were scheduled to finish Thursday before some matches were postponed until Friday because of rain. Potential women's contenders such as No. 11 Marta Kostyuk and No. 17 Alex Eala were among those waiting to see who they would face in their openers.

articles.title: UP Visayas' 1st chancellor dies at 105
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY— Dr. Dionisia A. Rola, the first chancellor of the University of the Philippines (UP Visayas) has died at the age of 105. The UP Visayas announced that Rola passed away on Wednesday…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY— Dr. Dionisia A. Rola, the first chancellor of the University of the Philippines (UP Visayas) has died at the age of 105.
The UP Visayas announced that Rola passed away on Wednesday evening, August 26.
Rola was a formidable force in the existence of UP in Iloilo when she started her career after UP Iloilo College (UPIC) was established in July 1947.

By the 1970s, Rola became the dean of the UP College Iloilo (UPCI) and envisioned the creation of an autonomous UP unit in the Visayas with its main campus in Miag-ao, a coastal town in Iloilo province.

“She lobbied for the creation of a new autonomous campus in the Visayas, requested a loan from the World Bank, and held coordination activities with concerned officials at the national and local levels for the lot acquisition,” the UP Visayas stated.
It was in 1980 when Executive Order No. 628 formally operationalized UP in the Visayas and Rola became its first chancellor.
Rola also had the distinction of becoming the first woman chancellor in the entire UP System.
Rola also established key arts and cultural programs for the university. It was through her initiatives that the Center for West Visayan Studies (CWVS) was created in June 1975.
Rola was also the brains behind what is now the UP Visayas Museum of Art and Cultural Heritage (MACH).
“Chancellor Rola helped shape UP Visayas into an institution committed to honor, excellence, service, and regional development,” stated the UP Visayas Alumni Association.

articles.title: Gunman behind killing of businesswoman in Ilocos Norte falls
articles.summary: SINAIT, Ilocos Sur — A 44-year-old man tagged as the prime suspect in the killing of a businesswoman in Badoc, Ilocos Norte was arrested after police raided his rented house here and seized a…

blocks.text: SINAIT, Ilocos Sur — A 44-year-old man tagged as the prime suspect in the killing of a businesswoman in Badoc, Ilocos Norte was arrested after police raided his rented house here and seized a .45-caliber pistol and 21 rounds of ammunition on Wednesday night, August 26.

The suspect, identified only as alias “Rod,” married, and a resident of Badoc, was arrested by personnel of the Sinait Municipal Police Station (MPS) during the implementation of a search warrant for alleged violation of Republic Act 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.
Police said “Rod” was linked to the August 21 gunslaying of alias “Liza,” a married businesswoman from Sitio Alalucap, Barangay Labut, Badoc, Ilocos Norte.
The search warrant was issued by the Regional Trial Court, First Judicial Region, Branch 24 in Cabugao, Ilocos Sur, following an application filed by the Sinait MPS.
Aside from the .45-caliber firearm and 21 rounds of ammunition, police also seized three .45-caliber magazines and a belt bag.
“Rod” is now facing charges for violation of RA 10591, while police continue to build their case over the businesswoman’s killing.

articles.title: Meta settles lawsuit for $18 billion
articles.summary: Meta, the owner of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and messaging app WhatsApp, has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle with the lawsuit filed against them across 29 US…

blocks.text: Meta, the owner of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and messaging app WhatsApp, has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle with the lawsuit filed against them across 29 US states.
The lawsuit alleged that Meta built their platforms to be addictive for children, even as it caused harm and impact of social media on them.

The amount 18 billion seems more like a slap to the wrist, since Meta has earned 200 billion last year. It is also the price they are willing to pay to not move the lawsuit into a jury trial. A jury trial would have meant a group of chosen ordinary citizens must listen to the facts of a trial and evaluate evidence presented, and it is them who will make a verdict. Whereas a settlement is where both parties have agreed to an outcome.

This is not a problem isolated within the digital walls of Meta alone, and Meta knows it. They posted a call to action to TikTok and YouTube to join them in protecting teens. It was the most “If we’re going down, you’re going down with me” kind of thing.

Developed with 52 state attorney generals, Meta will launch a set of protections, which include adding time limits on social media use, showing daily usage analytics, and prompts to encourage “intentional” use. That last one may mean encouraging teens to use social media only when they actually need to and not simply open the app and start doomscrolling.

Other protections include blocking notifications on times when the teens are supposed to be in school. Also, blocking the number of likes and reactions from their posts and others’ posts. “Extreme makeup filters” will also be blocked.
Meta will also invest in improving their age verification.

articles.title: Westmincom marks 20th anniversary
articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- The Western Mindanao Command marked its 20th founding anniversary on Thursday, August 27, at the gymnasium of Camp Don Basilio Navarro here with the theme "Strengthening Joint and…

blocks.text: ZAMBOANGA CITY- The Western Mindanao Command marked its 20th founding anniversary on Thursday, August 27, at the gymnasium of Camp Don Basilio Navarro here with the theme "Strengthening Joint and Inter-Agency Operations toward Resilient Western MIndanao."

The ceremony, graced by AFP Chief of Staff Gen. Antonio Nafarrete, brought together military personnel, government officials, partner agencies, veterans and other stakeholders to recognize two decades of service and sacrifice.

The program featured a live simulation exercise showcasing inter-agency defense operations. Awards were also given to officers, enlisted personnel, the Civilian Human Resource of the Year and other stakeholders in recognition of their contributions to the command.
The anniversary was the culmination of a series of activities including the Run-for-a Cause, Veterans’ Day, Interagency Territorial Defense Operations exercises, a wellness caravan, and others.
Maj. Gen. Jose Vladimir R. Cagara, acting commander of WESMINCOM, said the milestone also provides an opportunity to assess the command’s readiness amid an evolving security environment.
“Today, we celebrate 20 years of service, sacrifice, protecting our people, preserving peace, and defending this part of the nation,” Cagara said.

General Nafarrete thanked stakeholders for their continued support to WestMinCom and its units. He said the command will play a greater role this year in coordinating and harmonizing security efforts, strengthening communication and promoting a peaceful and orderly election process in coordination with the Philippine National Police and other government agencies.

The celebration underscored the continuing partnership among the military, government agencies, and local communities in protecting peace gains and building safer and more resilient communities across Western MIndanao.

articles.title: SuperManila Comic Con celebrates Filipino komiks legends with two exclusive classics
articles.summary: Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks. This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Luminaries and Life
Limited-edition releases of "Darna" and "Kaluluwa ni Dante" bring iconic works of Mars Ravelo and Francisco V. Coching closer to collectors
Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks.
(Photos: SuperManila Comic Con)

This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage with two highly collectible exclusive releases: “Classic Darna #1,” featuring the earliest adventures of Mars Ravelo's legendary heroine, and “Kaluluwa ni Dante,” a landmark masterpiece by the "King of Komiks," Francisco V. Coching.

Available exclusively at SuperManila Comic Con, these special editions allow longtime fans to revisit two Philippine comics classics while introducing their timeless stories and artwork to a new generation of collectors.
"Classic Darna #1" (in color and sepia) created by Mars Ravelo, illustrated by Nestor Redondo, exclusive cover artwork by Stanley "Artgerm" Lau
‘Classic Darna #1’: The legend returns!
Created by legendary Filipino komiks writer Mars Ravelo, Darna first appeared in Pilipino Komiks in 1950 and went on to become one of the Philippines' most enduring cultural icons.

“Classic Darna #1” SuperManila Comic Con Exclusive reprints stories from Darna's earliest komiks appearances, including her first appearance and legendary origin story. The original stories feature the breathtaking artwork of acclaimed Filipino artist Nestor Redondo, whose illustrations helped define Darna's iconic look for generations of readers.
Adding a stunning contemporary touch to this historic release, both editions feature exclusive cover artwork by internationally renowned artist Stanley "Artgerm" Lau.
The release comes in two strictly limited editions:

items: Full-Color Virgin Cover Edition — ₱1,000 per copy, 1,000 copies featuring the original stories presented in vibrant color.

Sepia Cover / Black-and-White Interior Edition — ₱800 per copy, 1,000 copies featuring a sepia-toned cover and the stories reproduced in black and white, paying tribute to the way generations of Filipino readers experienced Darna in the pages of komiks.

blocks.text: Every copy of both editions also includes an exclusive Darna trading card.
This is not a new story or retelling, but a reprint of the classic material that helped establish Darna's enduring legacy.
"Kaluluwa ni Dante" by Francisco V. Coching, the "King of Komiks," 116-page softcover edition, original black-and-white format, only 300 copies (₱1,000 per copy)
‘Kaluluwa ni Dante’: A masterpiece from the ‘King of Komiks’

Francisco V. Coching (1919–1998) is widely regarded as one of the greatest storytellers and illustrators in Philippine comics history. Hailed as the "King of Komiks," Coching created more than 50 serialized komiks novels over a career spanning four decades, including such celebrated works as “Pedro Penduko,” “Hagibis,” “Sabas, ang Barbaro,” “El Indio,” “Lapu-Lapu,” and “Kaluluwa ni Dante.”

First serialized in 1949, “Kaluluwa ni Dante” follows Dante Magtanggol on an extraordinary out-of-body journey guided by the mysterious Dr. Futiphar. Blending mystery, fantasy, adventure, and moral drama, the story explores justice, redemption, love, and the timeless struggle between good and evil.
With Coching's richly detailed artwork and cinematic storytelling, “Kaluluwa ni Dante” remains one of his most celebrated masterpieces.

Coching's influence extended far beyond komiks. Fifty-one of his 63 komiks novels were adapted into films, making him one of the most adapted creators in Philippine cinema. In 2014, he was posthumously conferred the title of National Artist for Visual Arts.
SuperManila Comic Con presents a special 116-page softcover edition of "Kaluluwa ni Dante," faithfully reproduced in its original black-and-white format, preserving Coching's timeless artwork.
Only 300 copies will be produced, making this a particularly rare opportunity for collectors and fans of Philippine komiks history.
Two legends. Two classics. One celebration of Philippine comics.

From “Darna,” the legendary heroine created by Mars Ravelo, to “Kaluluwa ni Dante,” the masterpiece of National Artist Francisco V. Coching, these exclusive SuperManila Comic Con releases celebrate the creators and stories that helped shape Filipino pop culture.

“Classic Darna #1” and “Kaluluwa ni Dante” will be available exclusively at the SMCC Merch Booth at The Concourse during SuperManila Comic Con 2026, from Sept. 4 to 6, 2026, at The Concourse and Space at One Ayala, Makati City.
For tickets and event updates, visit supermanila.ph and follow SuperManila Comic Con on its official social media channels.

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: Gokongwei takes PhilWeb helm amid AI gaming pivot
articles.summary: Tycoon Lance Y. Gokongwei has been named chairman of the board of directors of PhilWeb Corp. to mark the gaming company’s shift to a supplier of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled online gaming…

blocks.text: Tycoon Lance Y. Gokongwei has been named chairman of the board of directors of PhilWeb Corp. to mark the gaming company’s shift to a supplier of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled online gaming platforms to some of the country’s biggest casinos.

In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Friday, Aug. 28, PhilWeb said its board of directors approved the relinquishment by Crisanto Roy B. Alcid of his positions as chairman of the board and chief executive officer (CEO) of the corporation, effective Aug. 27, 2026. He will continue to serve as a director of the corporation.
The board also approved the appointment of Gokongwei, already a director of PhilWeb, as chairman of the board, effective Aug. 27, to serve for the remainder of Alcid’s term.

In a separate disclosure, the company said Gokongwei now directly owns 159.53 million shares, equivalent to a 15-percent stake, acquired at ₱8 apiece or a total of ₱2 billion pursuant to the share purchase agreement (SPA) executed last month.

PhilWeb said in a statement that this leadership transition completes the company’s governance restructuring, following Gokongwei’s recent ₱2.02-billion strategic equity investment and his appointment to the board in July.

It noted that the election signals PhilWeb’s definitive shift from capitalization to the aggressive, large-scale execution of its commercial online-led business-to-business (B2B) AI-enabled technology roadmap.

“This transition marks a critical inflection point for our capitalization and operational scale. Our objective is clear: to deploy institutional-grade, AI-powered infrastructure that establishes a new operational standard for security and compliance across the regulated digital ecosystem,” said Gokongwei.

Under Gokongwei’s strategic oversight, PhilWeb is accelerating the deployment of its enterprise AI layer. This technological pivot transitions the company into an institutional-grade digital gaming solutions provider.

The immediate operational mandate focuses on the integration of real-time operational monitoring, algorithmic risk management, regulatory compliance automation, anti-fraud detection, and data-driven customer lifecycle optimization.

“Having Lance Gokongwei step into the chairman role provides the institutional governance required for our next phase of scale. His strategic oversight ensures that our AI infrastructure rollout—specifically engineered to serve the complex backend needs of luxury integrated casino resorts and global platform providers—is executed with absolute capital market discipline,” said PhilWeb President Brian Ng.
The governance upgrade strengthens PhilWeb’s position as the foundational operational backbone for the regulated digital gaming sector.

The company’s AI-driven technology currently powers a premier, interconnected ecosystem of luxury integrated casino resorts and licensed operators, including Okada Manila, Hann Casino, Newport World Resorts, NUSTAR Resort and Casino, FBM Philippines, and PT Gaming.

Furthermore, PhilWeb continues to embed elite global content providers, such as Pragmatic Play and Games Global, into its unified digital infrastructure, securing deep commercial moats and operational dominance in the B2B market. - James A. Loyola

articles.title: Good Good out as PGA Tour title sponsor, Callaway deal ends
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Good Good Golf lost its partnership with Callaway on Thursday, Aug. 27, and no longer will be title sponsor of a PGA Tour event in November as the fallout continued over a video for a…

blocks.text: ATLANTA (AP) — Good Good Golf lost its partnership with Callaway on Thursday, Aug. 27, and no longer will be title sponsor of a PGA Tour event in November as the fallout continued over a video for a new Callaway driver that showed a man shoving a woman to the ground who was trying to touch the golf club.

Good Good, among the most popular in the YouTube Golf space, has said the video was meant to be a spinoff from the movie, “Obsession.” But the criticism was immediate and relentless, and the pressure began mounting by the day.
The video was deleted the same day it was posted on Aug. 20, but it continued to make the rounds on social media and apologies from Good Good and Callaway had little effect.
“We were disappointed with what we saw,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday of the response from Good Good. He said its role as a title sponsor was a “fluid situation.”

“We agree with their decision to use this time to focus on their organization and the work ahead,” the tour said in a statement Thursday. “The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all.”
The tournament already was changed on the PGA Tour's website to “Austin Championship.”

Golf Channel postponed a Good Good reality show Wednesday — “Big Break x Good Good” — because a sponsor, reported to be Galaxy Golf, wanted its brand scrubbed from the telecast. Dick's Sporting Goods removed the apparel from its stories. And then Callaway said it was ending the three-year sponsorship.
The PGA Tour confirmed Good Good said it would pull out as title sponsor of the new Nov. 12-15 tournament in Austin, Texas. The tour said the tournament still would be played.

“After thoughtful discussions with the PGA Tour and careful reflection, we have decided to step away as sponsor of the tour event in Austin this fall,” Good Good said in a social media post. “We recognize that we have work to do as an organization, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we will learn from this situation.”
Golf Channel announced Friday afternoon the Big Break x Good Good series would be scrapped this year. The winner was to have received a sponsor exemption to the Austin tournament.

“Following recent developments involving Good Good, and including the fact that the intended outcome of the series can no longer be fulfilled, Golf Channel will not be able to complete this season of Big Break as planned,” Golf Channel said in a statement.
It said Big Break would return next year.

In the 60-second video for Callaway’s new driver co-branded with Good Good, Garrett Clark shoves Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she reaches for the driver. As she is on the ground he leans over tells her, "Do not touch my new driver.”
Clark and Miestowski work for Good Good.

The video was pulled the night it was posted, and it was followed by apologies by Good Good Golf and Callaway Golf the next day. But then Callaway added another layer of apologies, this one from CEO Chip Brewer, who conceded that while Good Good produced the video, Callaway approved it before it was posted.
Brewer said the approval never should have happened and the company would investigate.

Callaway posted to its social media channels on Thursday that it has ended its relationship with Good Good effective immediately; has taken “appropriate internal corrective actions” and strengthened approval procedures to avoid another mistake; and has committed $1 million to support organizations working to prevent violence against women.
“These actions do not undo the harm caused or excuse our role in it,” the statement said. “We sincerely apologize to everyone who was hurt, disappointed, or offended by this incident.”

Good Good Golf was launched as a YouTube channel in 2020 and now is among the largest content creators in the sport, featuring eight men and four women competing in golf and various challenges. It has made-for-TV shows, apparel and other merchandise.
Clark, one of the Good Good founders, posted an eight-minute video Wednesday evening in which he called it “the worst ad known to man” and the reaction to the ad was “not what we stand for.”
“I do not support DV (domestic violence) or abuse or any of that of any kind," he said.
The PGA Tour has embraced such content creators over the last several years, even staging exhibitions during the week of The Players Championship and Tour Championship.

articles.title: Escudero: Free housing through government land usufruct will benefit millions of low-income Filipinos
articles.summary: Millions of low-income Filipinos stand to benefit on a proposed law that seeks to institutionalize free housing through usufruct, a legal arrangement that grants families the right to occupy and…

blocks.text: Millions of low-income Filipinos stand to benefit on a proposed law that seeks to institutionalize free housing through usufruct, a legal arrangement that grants families the right to occupy and enjoy government land and housing without owning them.

Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero pointed this out when he endorsed Senate Bill No. 2421 or the Free Housing Through Usufruct Act under Committee Report No. 79 on Wednesday, August 26. The bill is now pending second reading.

“Through usufruct, this bill seeks to grant Filipino families the right to occupy, use, and enjoy government land and improvements for residential purposes, while ownership remains with the State,” Escudero said of the measure.

Under the bill, only underprivileged, homeless citizens who do not own real property and have no affiliation with squatting syndicates will qualify, the chairman of the Senate Committee on Urban Planning, Housing and Resettlement further said.
Each usufruct agreement, Escudero said, will be covered by a written contract detailing rights and obligations, including maintenance of the property and payment of utilities.

“Section 5 outlines who may benefit from adequate and decent housing under this proposal: underprivileged Filipinos who do not own a home or real property, and who are not professional squatters or members of squatting syndicates,” Escudero said.

Under the bill, the housing units are strictly for residential use and warned that occupants cannot sell, transfer, mortgage, or rent out the units to others—acts that will cancel their right to use the property and ban them from government housing program for 10 years.
SB 2421 also requires registration of usufruct contracts with the Registry of Deeds, ensuring transparency and legal protection for beneficiaries.

Under the measure, the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) will monitor the implementation, while local government units (LGUs) will be tasked to manage properties and guarantee access to basic services.
Escudero said the bill is designed to prevent abuse while securing tenure for genuine beneficiaries.
“Each usufruct agreement is embodied in a written contract specifying the parties' rights and obligations, as well as the conditions for the continued use and enjoyment of the property,” he said.
According to the senator, the concept of usufruct dates back to Roman civil law but remains relevant today as a tool to address the persistent problem of homelessness.
“If usufruct is the right to use a property and enjoy its fruits, may this proposal yield adequate and decent housing for the millions of Filipinos in need,” he emphasized.

articles.title: Celebrating 20 years of local craft as Padday na Lima builds a sustainable future
articles.summary: Cagayan Valley’s vibrant craftsmanship, flavors, and entrepreneurial spirit have arrived in Alabang as the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Region 2 opened the 20th Padday na Lima Regional…

blocks.text: Cagayan Valley’s vibrant craftsmanship, flavors, and entrepreneurial spirit have arrived in Alabang as the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Region 2 opened the 20th Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair last Aug. 24, 2026, at Festival Mall. With more than 100 micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the region’s five provinces, this milestone fair invites shoppers to discover products that are proudly local and thoughtfully made with sustainability in mind.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

Carrying the theme “20 Years of Vibrant Hands: Crafting a Sustainable Legacy of Culture and Community,” this year’s Padday na Lima goes beyond showcasing products as it celebrates the hands, stories, skills, and communities that make them possible. From regional delicacies and handcrafted pieces to fashion, home products, and other unique finds, visitors can experience the many ways Cagayan Valley’s local enterprises are creating value while keeping culture and sustainability alive.

The celebration drew distinguished guests, including DTI Undersecretary Blesila A. Lantayona and Muntinlupa City Mayor Hon. Rozzano Rufino B. Biazon. Meanwhile, First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos and the PLGUs of Batanes, Cagayan, and Isabela conveyed their support for the trade fair. DTI Region 2 Regional Director Ma. Sofia G. Narag, CESO V, and Acting Assistant Regional Director Atty. Michael B. Paggabao welcomed them all to the celebration, along with other partners and guests.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

The Padday na Lima Website 2.0 was also relaunched, giving MSMEs another avenue to bring their products to customers through digital commerce. Meanwhile, DTI Region 2 and the Department of Tourism launched Lakbay Likha: A Creative Tourism Experience, opening new possibilities for local products and craftsmanship by connecting them with the region’s tourism destinations and experiences.

The spotlight also shone on enterprises making a difference through the Padday na Lima MSME Awards, which recognized businesses demonstrating innovation and sustainability. Adding flair to the celebration, the 20th Padday na Lima Fashion Show, “Hibla’t Habi ng Rehiyon Dos: Padday na Lima Collections,” transformed local materials and traditional craftsmanship into contemporary fashion under the creative direction of Nueva Vizcaya-born designer and Region 2 Creative Icon Michael Barassi.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

The opening festivities culminated in a ceremonial bamboo tapping and the launch of the Padday na Lima Song, followed by an exhibit tour that officially opened the seven-day fair to shoppers and visitors.

For 20 years, Padday na Lima has been bringing Cagayan Valley closer to wider markets while helping sustain the people, skills, traditions, and livelihoods behind every product. Now, it’s your turn to experience it. Visit Padday na Lima at Festival Mall until Aug. 30, 2026, and discover your next local favorite. Come and take home a piece of Cagayan Valley’s vibrant and sustainable story.

articles.title: Court rejects Tarlac lawmaker Rivera’s bid to consolidate 9 graft cases
articles.summary: 'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
Jansen Romero/Rappler
'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

items: The Sandiganbayan court rejected Representative Noel Rivera's request to consolidate his graft cases, citing that they involve different public works projects.
Rivera is accused of having an unlawful interest in Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which secured significant government contracts during his congressional term.
The court emphasized that consolidating the cases could lead to confusion and delays, as they involve separate contracts and are spread across multiple divisions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan has rejected Tarlac 3rd District Representative Noel Rivera’s bid to have his graft cases handled by just one court division, saying these involve different public works projects and that lumping them together could cause confusion and delays.

In two separate resolutions on Thursday, August 27, the Sandiganbayan’s 6th Division denied Rivera’s motion for consolidation. The ruling, made by associate justices Sarah Jane Fernandez, Kevin Narce Vivero and Lord Villanueva, rejected the congressman’s contention that the nine cases were similar and that having only one division handle them would save time and resources.

Rivera is accused of keeping an unlawful interest in the construction firm Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which bagged government projects worth millions of pesos while he was serving as a member of the House of Representatives.

blocks.caption: Congress, contractors, conflict, corruption: A list of Rappler exclusives

blocks.text: Rivera has been accused by Ombudsman Boying Remulla of being one of the so-called “congtractors,” or members of the House of Representatives who keep stakes in companies that bagged juicy public works contracts.
Prosecutors have also accused him of owning a 54.8% stake in Tarlac 3-G, while his wife, Evelyn, allegedly held another 45%.
An earlier Rappler report cited DPWH data showing that Tarlac 3-G had already been winning a large share of government projects in Tarlac even before Rivera became a congressman.
Since Rivera entered Congress, Tarlac 3-G has secured P671 million worth of DPWH projects. The company reported total assets of P392 million in its 2024 financial statement.
Rivera’s cases were spread across six Sandiganbayan divisions, with the 5th, 6th and 7th divisions handling two cases each, while the 1st, 2nd and 4th divisions each took on one.
The court stressed that there was little chance of conflicting rulings because the cases involved separate contracts.

The cases involve contracts that Tarlac 3-G secured while Rivera was already serving as a congressman, with eight coming from the DPWH, while the Philippine State College of Aeronautics awarded the remaining contract.
“Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,” read part of the Sandiganbayan ruling. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Eala, seeded No. 17, takes on qualifier at US Open first round
articles.summary: Alex Eala is ready to take the US Open by storm as the No. 17 seed -- her highest-ever Grand Slam seeding -- clashes with a qualifier at Flushing Meadows. Her historic seeding, surpassing her…

blocks.text: Alex Eala is ready to take the US Open by storm as the No. 17 seed -- her highest-ever Grand Slam seeding -- clashes with a qualifier at Flushing Meadows.

Her historic seeding, surpassing her previous No. 25 mark at Wimbledon, places her in the bottom half of a loaded draw packed with dangerous elite opponents standing in her path that include last year’s finalist and 10th seed Amanda Anisimova.
A first-round victory would arrange the 21-year-old Filipina star a duel with the winner between Oleksandra Oliynykova of Ukraine and wildcard Reese Brantmeier of the United States.
Eala recently faced Oliynykova at the WTA 500 event in Strasbourg, France last May, falling to the Ukrainian in a three-set battle in the opening round.
The Filipina, however, has never faced Brantmeier on the WTA tour.

Other notable potential opponents for Eala deeper in the draw are good friend and 14th seed Iva Jovic, two-time Grand Slam doubles quarterfinalist Anastasia Potapova, 2017 French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko and 19-year-old reigning French Open champion Mirra Andreeva.
Of course, no path is easy at any Grand Slam as Eala is expected to go all out to eclipse her best Grand Slam showing of a fourth-round finish at the Wimbledon a few months ago.

Eala is carrying the momentum of an impressive North American swing campaign where she captured her breakthrough WTA title at the Mubadala DC Open, slaying giants like Zheng Qinwen, last year's champion Leylah Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka and 2024 US Open finalist Jessica Pegula.
She is also coming off a mixed doubles stint with Canadian Felix Auger-Aliassime, where they lost to spouses Gael Monfils and Svitolina.

articles.title: ‘Habagat’ to bring heavy rains during long weekend — PAGASA
articles.summary: Those looking forward to the long weekend may have to adjust their plans as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of the country, particularly western Luzon.…

blocks.text: Those looking forward to the long weekend may have to adjust their plans as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of the country, particularly western Luzon.

Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) weather specialist Obet Badrina said Friday, Aug. 28 that significant rainfall may prevail over Ilocos Region, Bataan, Zambales, parts of Calabarzon, Metro Manila, Oriental Mindoro, and Occidental Mindoro.
Heavy rains are expected to continue through Saturday, Aug. 29, and Sunday, Aug. 30, although they may ease by Sunday afternoon or Monday, Aug. 31, National Heroes Day.

“Partikular na sa Sabado at Linggo, inaasahan natin na magiging tuloy-tuloy ang mga malalakas na pag-ulan. Posibleng mabawasan po yan bandang hapon ng Linggo o Lunes na. Kaya sa mga kababayan natin na may activity this coming long weekend ay consider nating yung ineexpect na mga malalakas na pag-ulan lalong-lalo na sa western section nga ng western section ng Luzon (We expect the heavy rains to continue particularly on Saturday and Sunday. These may ease by Sunday afternoon or Monday. Those with activities this coming long weekend should consider the expected heavy rains, particularly over western Luzon),” Badrina said.
The rest of Luzon and Visayas may have scattered rains and thunderstorms, while Mindanao may generally have partly cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms.
The low-pressure area (LPA), designated LPA 08i, was enhancing the habagat as it was located 720 kilometers east of Itbayat, Batanes as of 3 a.m. Friday.
The LPA could still develop into a tropical cyclone this weekend but is not expected to make landfall in the Philippines.

“Posible pa rin ito maging bagyo this coming weekend pero hindi na ito magkakaroon ng direktang epekto sa ating bansa. Hindi ito inaasahang maglandfall sa Pilipinas at ang magiging direksyon nitong low-pressure area na kung sakaling maging bagyo ay sa may bahagi naman ng Taiwan (It is still possible for this to become a tropical cyclone this coming weekend, but it will no longer have a direct effect on our country. It is not expected to make landfall in the Philippines, and if it becomes a tropical cyclone, the low-pressure area is expected to move toward Taiwan),” Badrina said.
If LPA 08i develops into a tropical depression, it will be given the local name “Pilandok.”
Another LPA could form next week and may further strengthen the habagat, Badrina said, citing PAGASA’s two-week tropical cyclone threat potential forecast.

“Around August 27 to September 2, inaasahan na ang low-pressure area na ating minomonitor ay patungo sa bahagi ng Taiwan. Samantala, by next week posibleng may mabuo na panibagong low-pressure area at maaaring magpatuloy na magpalakas ng habagat hanggang next week (Around August 27 to September 2, the low-pressure area we are monitoring is expected to move toward Taiwan. Meanwhile, by next week, another low-pressure area may form and could continue to strengthen the habagat into next week),” Badrina said.
He advised the public to continue monitoring PAGASA updates as longer-range forecasts are less certain and may still change.

blocks.text: There is something about spring that makes everything feel possible again. For Gucci, that sense of renewal becomes the starting point of its latest campaign, Gucci Primavera—the first campaign unveiled under the creative direction of Demna.

blocks.caption: Ningning of Aespa, Jin of BTS, and Xiao Zhan for Gucci Primavera (Photos: Gucci)

blocks.text: Ningning of Aespa, Jin of BTS, and Xiao Zhan for Gucci Primavera (Photos: Gucci)

Celebrating rebirth through the transformative power of love, the campaign brings together a stellar global cast of 10 talents from across entertainment, fashion, music, and sport, with Asian representation taking center stage.

Chinese actor Xiao Zhan joins South Korean stars Jin of BTS and Ningning of Aespa, alongside acclaimed actress Lee Young Ae and model and rapper Tarzzan. The global lineup continues with Canadian singer Shawn Mendes, American model Alex Consani, football icon Tom Brady, rapper Rico Nasty, and British rapper EsDeeKid—a deliberately eclectic group that reflects the many facets of Gucci’s evolving identity.
Lee Young-ae
Tarzzan
EsDeeKid
Tom Brady
Rico Nasty

Photographed by Michal Chelbin, the talents appear in looks from Demna’s debut Gucci collection, introducing a new vocabulary of silhouettes and textures. There is an ease to the styling, with pieces designed to move across different modes of dressing while retaining the house’s unmistakable codes. Heritage is present, but it feels reframed rather than revisited—a contemporary interpretation of Gucci through Demna’s lens.
And then there is love.

Bringing the campaign’s emotional narrative to life is a short film featuring fashion icon Kate Moss, who lip-syncs to Chris Isaak’s haunting “Wicked Game.” The visuals are romantic, slightly surreal, and deliberately cinematic, a fitting introduction to a campaign built around the idea of awakening. Much like spring itself, Gucci Primavera is about what happens when something dormant begins to stir: new energy, new encounters, and the possibility of falling in love all over again.
