articles.title: Prompt, fair case resolution builds public trust -- Chief Justice Gesmundo
articles.summary: Supreme Court Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on Saturday stressed the importance of resolving cases fairly and promptly, saying the efficient administration of justice is crucial to maintaining…

blocks.text: Published August 8, 2026 10:46pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Supreme Court Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on Saturday stressed the importance of resolving cases fairly and promptly, saying the efficient administration of justice is crucial to maintaining public confidence in the judiciary.
In a “24 Oras Weekend” report on Saturday, Gesmundo said cases can have a significant impact on Filipinos’ quality of life, livelihoods, and human rights.

“Justice delayed is not merely an administrative difficulty. For this reason, efficiency is not simply a matter of procedure; it is a responsibility of justice itself,” Gesmundo said in a speech at the Manila Overseas Press Club Judiciary Night.
“The judiciary must continue to ensure that cases are resolved fairly, promptly, and through processes that are transparent, reliable, and worthy of public confidence,” he added.
Gesmundo also stressed the importance of judicial independence, saying it cannot be sustained if judges and court personnel face intimidation or threats.
He highlighted ongoing judicial reforms aimed at making courts more efficient, accessible, and responsive to the needs of the public.

Among these initiatives are the establishment of a Code of Conduct and Accountability for members of the judiciary and court employees, as well as the creation of the Office of the Regional Court Manager. — Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Iba't ibang bahagi ng bansa, binaha dahil sa ulan na dulot ng Habagat
articles.summary: Nakaranas ng malalakas na pag-ulan ang malaking bahagi ng bansa dulot ng Habagat, na nagdulot ng pagbaha sa ilang bahagi ng Metro Manila at iba pang lugar sa Luzon.

blocks.text: Nakaranas ng malalakas na pag-ulan ang malaking bahagi ng bansa dulot ng Habagat, na nagdulot ng pagbaha sa ilang bahagi ng Metro Manila at iba pang lugar sa Luzon.

Sa ulat ni Jonathan Andal sa "24 Oras Weekend" nitong Sabado, sinuong ng mga rescuer sa Barangay Tulay, Odiongan, Romblon ang rumaragasang baha upang sagipin ang mga pamilyang na-stranded noong madaling araw.
Isang senior citizen ang iniahon gamit ang lubid at salbabida mula sa abot-dibdib na baha.
Nagsagawa na rin ng evacuation ang mga awtoridad sa mga mabababa at bahaing lugar dahil sa malakas na ulan. Nanatili sa evacuation center ang mga residenteng inilikas.
Sa Sablayan, Occidental Mindoro, mistulang ilog ang isang kalsada dahil sa mataas na baha kasunod ng malakas na ulan.
Ilang motorista ang na-stranded, habang pinilit naman ng iba na suungin ang baha. Nahihirapang makadaan ang maliliit na sasakyan.
Sa Batangas City, nasira ang pundasyon ng isang tulay sa Barangay Santo Niño.
Pinayuhan ang mga motorista na dumaan muna sa alternatibong ruta bilang pag-iingat.
Hiniling ni Batangas City Mayor Marvey Mariño sa Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) ang agarang pagpapatayo ng bagong tulay.
Bumaha rin sa J.P. Laurel Highway sa Batangas City, ngunit sinuong pa rin ito ng ilang sasakyan. Ilang residente rin ang na-stranded.
Sa San Marcelino, Zambales, umapaw ang ilog at binaha ang ilang bahagi ng Barangay Santa Fe.
Halos umabot sa bubong ng isang paaralan ang baha.
Ayon sa Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO), walang naiulat na nasawi o nasugatan dahil sa pag-apaw ng ilog.
Sinuspinde naman ng Philippine Coast Guard ang pangingisda at paglalayag ng ilang sasakyang pandagat sa Zambales dahil sa masamang lagay ng dagat.
Nagkaroon din ng pagguho ng lupa sa Barangay Santa Rita sa Olongapo City, kung saan isang bahay ang naapektuhan.
Naitala rin ang landslide sa bahagi ng Tagaytay-Talisay Road sa Barangay San Jose, Tagaytay City, Cavite, gayundin sa bahagi ng national road sa Barangay San Miguel, Lobo, Batangas.
Ayon sa PAGASA, ang Habagat ang nagdadala ng ulan sa malaking bahagi ng bansa.
Samantala, sa hiwalay na ulat ni Bernadette Reyes, mistulang may bagyo sa lakas ng ulan at hangin sa Timog Avenue at Commonwealth Avenue sa Quezon City noong Sabado ng umaga.
Sa Barangay Roxas District sa Quezon City, ilang dekada nang problema ang pagbaha ngunit patuloy pa rin itong nararanasan ng mga residente.
Bagama’t saglit lamang bumuhos ang malakas na ulan, umabot pa rin hanggang dibdib ang baha sa ilang lugar.
Isang lalaki ang gumamit ng styrofoam na balsa upang makatawid sa hanggang-bewang na baha, habang ang ilan ay gumamit pa ng bangka upang makauwi sa kanilang mga bahay.
Umabot naman hanggang dibdib ang baha sa ibang bahagi ng kalsada.
Sa kabila ng panganib na magkasakit, ilang kabataan ang naligo sa baha.
Bumaha rin sa ilang bahagi ng Quezon Avenue at D. Tuazon Street.
Sa Barangay Tatalon, nagpatuloy ang hanapbuhay at negosyo ng ilang residente sa kabila ng abot-dibdib na baha.
Halos mag-zero visibility naman sa ilang bahagi ng Metro Manila nitong tanghali, batay sa kuha ni YouScooper Mina mula sa kanyang condominium unit sa Makati City.
Sa Bauan, Batangas, dahan-dahang dumaan ang mga sasakyan sa isang kalsadang lubog sa abot-tuhod na baha.
Sa kuha naman ni YouScooper Kimberly mula sa Batangas City, umabot hanggang binti ang baha bunsod ng walang tigil na pag-ulan.
Itinaas nitong alas-5 ng hapon ang Red Rainfall Warning sa Metro Manila, Batangas, at iba pang bahagi ng Luzon. — Jamil Santos/MCG GMA News

articles.title: Reticulated python, namataan sa mga stuffed toy sa ukayan sa Dumaguete
articles.summary: Nasagip ang isang reticulated python o sawa na natagpuang nakahalo sa mga stuffed toy sa isang ukayan sa Dumaguete.

blocks.text: Nasagip ang isang reticulated python o sawa na natagpuang nakahalo sa mga stuffed toy sa isang ukayan sa Dumaguete.
Batay sa impormasyon GMA Regional TV, na iniulat sa 24 Oras Weekend nitong Sabado, mapanonood sa video ang pagsagip ng mga kawani ng BFP sa ahas.
Tinatayang nasa apat hanggang limang talampakan ang haba ng sawa at may bigat na halos tatlong kilo.
Sinabi ng BFP na naunang napansin ng isang customer na may makinis na bagay sa kahon ng mga ibinibentang stuffed toys.
Nai-turnover na ang sawa sa DENR. —Jamil Santos/VBL GMA News

articles.title: 3 sa 5 Chinese na sangkot sa tangkang pagdukot sa kapwa Chinese at paghingi ng mahigit P60M ransom, huli
articles.summary: Arestado ang tatlo sa limang Chinese dahil sa tangkang pagdukot sa kapwa nila Chinese at panghihingi ng mahigit P60 milyon ransom sa Angeles, Pampanga.

blocks.text: Arestado ang tatlo sa limang Chinese dahil sa tangkang pagdukot sa kapwa nila Chinese at panghihingi ng mahigit P60 milyon ransom sa Angeles, Pampanga.
Sa ulat ni John Consulta sa 24 Oras Weekend nitong Sabado, mapanonood ang biglang pagharang ng isang puting van sa likuran ng isang umaatras na itim na SUV sa isang establisimyento.
Ilang saglit pa, bumaba mula sa van ang limang armadong lalaki, tinutukan at puwersahang hinatak palabas ang driver ng SUV at isinakay ito sa kanilang puting van.
Lumabas sa imbestigasyon ng pulisya na isang Chinese ang driver ng SUV, pati na rin ang mga armadong lalaki.

“Inabangan nila at noong nakasakay na sila sa van, nu’ng paalis na itong sasakyan, nu’ng sumakay na ng sasakyan itong Chinese, isa doon sa mga suspek ay nakasuot ng camouflage. At kung titignan mo ‘yung galawan nila, napakabilis. Very swift 'yung ginawa nilang pagkuha. At 'yung modus sila, makikita mo, isinalin sa ibang sasakyan, inikot-ikot, then siyempre na-ready na nila 'yung safe house, kung saan nila dadalhin. Chinese to Chinese ang nangyari. So ang puntirya nila is Chinese,” sabi ni Police Brigadier General Jess Mendez, Regional Director, PRO3.
Nahanap at nadakip sa Tarlac City ang tatlo sa limang Chinese na dumukot sa kanilang kababayan sa follow-up operation ng RSOG 3 at PNP Anti-Kidnapping Group kinabukasan.
Isang Pilipina din ang dinakip na nagrenta ng puting van na ginamit sa pagdukot.
Nasagip ng PNP Region 3 at AKG sa Angeles, Pampanga ang biktima, na nakaposas pa nang tumakas sa mga safe house ng grupo sa Mabalacat, Pampanga.
Sinabi ng PNP Region 3 na may kaanak din sa bansa ang biktima at siyam na araw pa lang siyang narito nang dukutin.
Isang milyong dolyar o katumbas ng mahigit P60 milyon ang hinihinging ransom ng mga Chinese kidnapper.

“'Yung nagne-negotiate, going from one place to another, paikot-ikot lang sa area ng Clark, Angeles, then Tarlac. Based on our investigation, isa doon ay may kaso dati sa China na parang scam sa mga illegal gambling. And the other one, ang remarks nila is drug addict,” sabi ni Mendez.
Hindi pa nagbibigay ng pahayag ang mga suspek.
Na-turnover na ang mga nadakip na suspek sa PNP Anti-Kidnapping Group habang nasampahan sila ng reklamong kidnapping sa Department of Justice. —Jamil Santos/VBL GMA News

articles.title: Baguio tourists unfazed by Habagat rains
articles.summary: Despite the inclement weather brought by the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, some tourists in Baguio City braved the cold winds and heavy rains to push through with their travel plans.

blocks.text: Published August 8, 2026 9:53pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
Despite the inclement weather brought by the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, some tourists in Baguio City braved the cold winds and heavy rains to push through with their travel plans.
In a “24 Oras Weekend” report by Marisol Abdurahman on Saturday, a local hotel said it was nearly fully booked, with most guests coming from nearby lowland provinces.
“This weekend, po sir, almost fully booked po tayo. Most of our guests are families na galing po sa mga taga-baba, mga probinsya,” hotel staff member Daisy Savellano said.
(This weekend, sir, we are almost fully booked. Most of our guests are families from the lowlands and nearby provinces.)
Other Stories
Among those who pushed through with their vacation despite the bad weather was the family of an overseas Filipino worker (OFW).
“Sabi ko, ano na lang, God forbid, walang mangyari sa amin. So ganon lang—ang isang OFW, na naghahanap ng kasiyahan din,” the OFW said.
“Four weeks lang kami dito, but nung dumating kami sa ano, since nung touchdown namin umuulan na,” he added.

(I just prayed, God forbid, that nothing bad would happen to us. That's just how it is for an OFW who also wants to enjoy some time off. We're only here for four weeks, but it has been raining since we arrived.)
Another family also decided to push through with their trip to celebrate a child's birthday.
“Birthday po kasi ng anak ko bukas, so kahit umuulan, okay lang, go,” another tourist said.
(It's my child's birthday tomorrow, so even if it's raining, it's fine—we're still going.)
The persistent rains, however, caused flooding and other incidents in Baguio City and nearby areas.
A portion of Naguilian Road in Barangay Irisan was flooded, while a house in the same barangay was reportedly hit by falling bamboo.
In Camp 7, a fallen tree damaged another house. Meanwhile, in Atok, Benguet, video footage showed muddy floodwaters rushing down a highway.
In Mountain Province, large boulders fell onto a section of the Bontoc-Kalinga National Road, prompting authorities to warn motorists to remain vigilant amid the threat of landslides.

In Benguet, the Ambuklao and Binga dams also began releasing water. According to PAGASA's Hydrometeorology Division, both dams were nearing their normal high water levels as of 8 a.m. due to persistent rains. — Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: First alarm raised as Marikina River water level hits 15 meters
articles.summary: Local authorities raised the first alarm after the water level in the Marikina River reached 15 meters on Saturday evening amid heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published August 8, 2026 9:46pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

blocks.caption: First alarm raised as Marikina River water level hits 15 meters

blocks.text: Courtesy: Marikina PIO
Local authorities raised the first alarm after the water level in the Marikina River reached 15 meters on Saturday evening amid heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).
According to the Marikina Public Information Office, the water level stood at 15.3 meters as of 9 p.m.
The first alarm means residents should prepare for possible evacuation.

Preemptive evacuation will be implemented when the water level reaches 16 meters, triggering the second alarm. When the water level reaches 18 meters, the third alarm will be raised, signaling mandatory evacuation. —VBL, GMA News
Other Stories

articles.title: 3 Chinese kidnapping suspects nabbed, charged at DOJ
articles.summary: Kidnapping charges have been filed with the Department of Justice (DOJ) against several Chinese nationals accused of abducting a fellow Chinese national and demanding US$1 million (about P60 million)…

blocks.text: Published August 8, 2026 9:39pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Kidnapping charges have been filed with the Department of Justice (DOJ) against several Chinese nationals accused of abducting a fellow Chinese national and demanding US$1 million (about P60 million) in ransom.

According to a "24 Oras Weekend" report by John Consulta on Saturday, CCTV footage showed the suspects using a white van to block the victim's car before pointing a gun at him and dragging him into their vehicle.
The victim was taken to a safehouse in Mabalacat, Pampanga, but later managed to escape from his captors. Authorities subsequently rescued him in Angeles City.
The kidnappers allegedly demanded US$1 million for his release.
Other Stories
The victim, who has relatives in the Philippines, had been in the country for only six days when he was abducted.
Police Regional Office 3 (PRO3) Regional Director Police Brigadier General Jess Mendez said the group's modus operandi was clear and that the suspects moved quickly.
“Chinese to Chinese ang nangyari (What happened involved Chinese nationals on both sides)," Mendez said.
In a follow-up operation, police arrested three of the five Chinese suspects in Tarlac City. Authorities also arrested the Filipino woman who allegedly rented the white van used in the kidnapping.
Mendez said one of the suspects had a previous case in China linked to scam operations, while another was allegedly involved in illegal drug use.
The arrested suspects are now in the custody of the Philippine National Police Anti-Kidnapping Group and face kidnapping charges. — Jean Mangaluz/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: 6 napaulat na nasawi dahil sa Bagyong Luis at Maymay, Habagat -- OCD
articles.summary: Umabot na sa anim ang napaulat na bilang ng mga nasawi dahil sa epekto ng Habagat (Habagat), at mga bagyong Luis at Maymay, ayon sa Office of Civil Defense nitong Sabado.

blocks.text: Umabot na sa anim ang napaulat na bilang ng mga nasawi dahil sa epekto ng Habagat (Habagat), at mga bagyong Luis at Maymay, ayon sa Office of Civil Defense nitong Sabado.

"In terms of casualties, mayroon na tayong bina-validate na 6. Dalawa sa Rodriguez, Rizal; dalawa sa Benguet, at mayroong dalawa sa La Union," sabi ni OCD Deputy Administrator and Assistant Secretary Bernardo Rafaelito Alejandro IV sa isang panayam sa Dobol B TV.
Mayroong pitong naiulat na sugatan sa Benguet na kasalukuyan pang bineberipika, ayon sa kaniya.
"Tuloy-tuloy pa rin nating nararanasan ang Southwest Monsoon lalo na sa norte, sa Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra, Benguet and parts of Region 3, even hanggang Mindoro," ani Alejandro.
"As of this morning, mayroon na tayong 74,800 families or 261,000 persons na apektado sa weather system na ito," dagdag niya
Mayroong 2,500 pamilya ang nasa 83 evacuation centers habang mahigit 2,200 indibiduwal ang nananatili sa labas ng mga evacuation centers, ayon sa opisyal ng OCD.

"Nagbibigay tulong tayo in terms of making sure na ma-evacuate 'yung mga nasa river tributaries (sa Pangasinan) dahil tuloy-tuloy ang pagbaba ng tubig galing sa mga bundok sa CAR... Tuloy-tuloy pa ang pag-uulan. Hindi tayo titigil sa pagbibigay ng ayuda doon at pagmo-monitor," sabi ni Alejandro.

Kaugnay naman ng mga pagbaha, 63 na lugar ang naiulat na binaha. Karamihan sa mga ito ang nasa Region 1 at 3 at sa ilang bahagi ng Calabarzon. Hindi pa rin madaanan ang ilang bahagi ng kalsada dahil sa pagbaha.
Napaulat din ang mga pagguho ng lupa sa Region 1 at sa Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), ani Alejandro.
"'Yung mga may balak na pumunta ng Baguio at Cordillera, hindi pa advisable na umakyat kasi may mga landslide at rockslide sa Benguet," sabi niya.
"In terms of damage naman, 120 houses ang reported na damage sa Region 1, CAR at Region 3," dagdag niya.
Nagkansela ng mga biyahe sa dagat ang 13 daungan sa Regions 1, 3, 5, at MIMAROPA, ayon sa opisyal ng OCD.

Samantala, sinabi ng Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) na namahagi ito ng tulong pinansyal sa mga pamilyang naapektuhan ng landslide sa Benguet at rockslide sa Rizal na dulot ng mga pag-ulan mula sa bagyong Maymay at ng pinalakas na Southwest Monsoon, o Habagat.
Dalawa katao ang patay at isa pa ang malubhang nasugatan matapos tumama ang landslide sa isang kainan sa Barangay Shilan, La Trinidad, Benguet, noong Agosto 6.
Sa Rodriguez, Rizal, dalawa katao ang patay matapos ang pag-ulan ng monsoon na nagdulot ng rockslide na tumama sa ilang bahay sa Barangay Wawa noong Miyerkules, Agosto 5.
Makararanas ng mga pag-ulan ang Luzon at Visayas sa loob ng susunod na 24 oras dahil sa Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), ayon sa PAGASA nitong Sabado ng umaga.
Magpapatuloy ang mga pag-ulan dulot ng Habagat hanggang sa susunod na linggo, ayon sa state weather bureau.
Lumabas na sa kalupaan ng Pilipinas ang Tropical Depression Maymay noong Huwebes ng hapon, humina at naging low pressure area noong Agosto 7.
Samantala, nawala naman ang tropical depression na si Luis noong Agosto 4. —Jamil Santos/VBL GMA News

articles.title: NCIP holds dialogue with Aeta community in Tarlac over Pax Silica
articles.summary: The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) held a dialogue with the Aeta Hungey Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) in Sitio Binyayan, Capas, Tarlac, to hear and…

blocks.text: The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) held a dialogue with the Aeta Hungey Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) in Sitio Binyayan, Capas, Tarlac, to hear and address their concerns about the proposed Pax Silica Project.

In a Facebook post, the NCIP said its Secretary and Chairperson Nancy Catamco, Ethnographic Commissioner for Region III and the Rest of Luzon Rhodex Valenciano, and other agency representatives visited the Aeta community.

“Tapat na iniharap ng mga kinatawan ng ICCs/IPs ang kanilang mga alalahanin, mula sa posibleng pagkagambala sa kanilang mga tirahan at kabuhayan, hanggang sa kanilang ancestral domain claim,” the NCIP said.
(Representatives of the ICCs/IPs candidly raised their concerns, ranging from possible disruptions to their homes and livelihoods to their ancestral domain claims.)
Other Stories

“Direktang tiniyak ng NCIP sa mga komunidad: hindi mababale-wala ang mga hinaing na ito. Ipaaabot ito sa Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), kasama ang kahilingan para sa sapat at malinaw na impormasyon tungkol sa Pax Silica Project,” the agency said.

(The NCIP directly assured the communities that these concerns would not be ignored. They will be relayed to the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), along with a request for sufficient and clear information about the Pax Silica Project.)

The dialogue was attended by local government leaders and indigenous representatives, including Capas Mayor Atty. Boots Rodriguez, Municipal IPMR Antonio Gutierrez, Sapang Kawayan Chieftain Petronilla Capiz Munoz, Barangay Aranguren IPMR Judith Lasquite, former IPO Chairman and Pagmimiha AD James Dela Cruz, Barangay Cut-cut II IPMR Analyn Aquino, Barangay Kagawad Gilbert Rueda, former Commissioner Bayani Sumaoang, Asosasyon ng mga Katutubo sa Mahawang President Casamira Maniego, and Binastro Julian.

“Bahagi ito ng patuloy na pagkilos ng NCIP upang matiyak na napapangalagaan at naipagtatanggol ang mga karapatan at kapakanan ng mga apektadong Katutubong Pamayanan. Bilang pangunahing ahensiyang may mandatong protektahan at isulong ang mga karapatan ng ICCs/IPs, patuloy na tututukan ng NCIP ang mga susunod na hakbang kaugnay ng Pax Silica Project at titiyaking naririnig at isinasaalang-alang ang boses at karapatan ng mga komunidad na maaapektuhan,” the agency said.

(This is part of the NCIP’s continuing efforts to ensure that the rights and welfare of affected Indigenous Communities are protected and upheld. As the primary agency mandated to protect and promote the rights of ICCs/IPs, the NCIP will continue to closely monitor the next steps concerning the Pax Silica Project and ensure that the voices and rights of affected communities are heard and taken into consideration.)
“Gagawin ng komisyon ang lahat ng nararapat na aksyon upang matiyak na mapangangalagaan ang boses, karapatan, at kapakanan ng mga Ayta Hungey, alinsunod sa umiiral na batas,” it added.
(The commission will take all necessary actions to ensure that the voices, rights, and welfare of the Ayta Hungey are protected in accordance with existing laws.)

Pax Silica is the US Department of State's flagship initiative on artificial intelligence and supply chain security, aimed at advancing a new economic security framework among allies and trusted partners.

The Philippines in April officially joined the Pax Silica initiative, cementing its place among other 23 global signatories, including the European Union, Japan, India, Singapore, South Korea, and the United Kingdom
As part of the initiative, Manila and Washington are working to establish a 4,000-acre industrial hub that is envisioned as a new model for AI-focused investment within the Luzon Economic Corridor.
The Pax Silica project is being criticized by many green groups for the massive amounts of energy and water it will likely consume once built.
Some groups have alleged that the project could displace agricultural land and indigenous communities.
The government, however, has continuously defended the project, reiterating that it will generate jobs and income.
The Marcos administration said no farmers will be displaced by the proposed Pax Silica project in Tarlac, noting that the site has been designated as a “buildable zone” since 2019. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: From his quiet home to a shooting spree at school, a Thai teenager's deadly rampage
articles.summary: The boy shot his grandparents dead at dawn on Friday in their two-storey house bordering rice fields on the outskirts of Bangkok. Each was killed by a single gunshot to the head, a Thai police…

blocks.text: BANG BUA THONG, Thailand — The boy shot his grandparents dead at dawn on Friday in their two-storey house bordering rice fields on the outskirts of Bangkok. Each was killed by a single gunshot to the head, a Thai police official said.
By noon, bodies lay strewn at the 14-year-old's school — five more dead and 23 wounded — before he turned the gun on himself, ending Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022.
Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong, superintendent of Bang Bua Thong Police Station, said the boy killed his elderly relatives at around 5 a.m. local time (2200 GMT Thursday).
"The firearm and the bullets belonged to the grandfather," Thadsakorn told Reuters. "An initial inspection found signs that the firearm had been searched for inside the grandfather's bedroom."
Other Stories
The three of them lived together in the house in Bang Bua Thong, surrounded by trees and ringed by a concrete fence in a quiet neighbourhood, a 90-minute drive from central Bangkok.
A canal runs by at the front and an empty plot of land lies behind. In the yard hangs a red and white Nazi flag that police said belonged to the teenager's uncle.
The whereabouts of the boy's parents remain unclear.
After shooting his grandparents, the teenager boarded the school van that came to fetch him at home, said Thadsakorn. He carried the gun and dozens of bullets with him.

The Debsirin Nonthaburi School, where the boy studied, lies around 18 km (11 miles) from the house, or a 45-minute drive. Last year, the school had an enrolment of around 3,100 students, taught by 147 teachers, according to district authorities.
His first class began at 8:30 a.m., followed by another at 9:20 a.m.
About half an hour into the boy's second class of the day he drew out the gun and began shooting again, police estimate.
At 9:57 a.m., the Plai Bang Police Station overseeing the area where the school is located received a phone call about a shooting, an official said.

As the shots rang out, one 18-year-old student initially thought he was hearing fireworks going off, before a teacher told him to evacuate. Some ran out in their socks or bare feet, clutching sheets of paper and mobile phones.
Others took cover under their desks, weeping as they lay on the floor listening to the sound of the firing, according to a video posted on social media and verified by Reuters.
Teachers targeted

The teenager is believed to have first shot teachers on the sixth floor of the building where he studied, killing three of them, said Police Major General Dejrapee Kongdee, commander of the Nonthaburi Provincial Police.

One was a female Thai language teacher who he shot in the eye, according to a timeline of the incident shared by Thai police. The gunman then appears to have continued down a corridor, shooting at students.
"He then walked down the stairs and encountered the school's deputy director and the director's secretary, who were going up the stairs to check on the situation," Dejrapee told Reuters.
"The attacker shot and killed both of them on the staircase."
The boy began walking towards another building but appeared to change his route after seeing police arrive, and he fled into a four-storey structure, Dejrapee said.
When he arrived at the school, emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, said the scene was chaotic as his team began treating students with wounds to the back, chest and arms.
"We were evaluating the sort of weapons he had," he said, referring to the gunman. "Therefore, we could not rush inside. The police then took a team with shields up there."

After evacuating students and teachers from the school, police began clearing the building floor-by-floor, until they found the teenager on the fourth floor, where he had already shot himself, said Dejrapee. The time was around 10:40 a.m.
"He was still alive, so they performed CPR and rushed him to the hospital," he said.
The 14-year-old died soon after.
In all, he had used at least 26 bullets. Another 34 rounds were found in his possession.
'Stressed from his studies'
The boy's motives remain unclear.

"He was stressed from his studies," Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters after he visited the school, echoing what one police official told Reuters. "His actions were deliberate. From what we saw he had a plan."
After the Songkran festival in April marking the start of Thailand's traditional New Year, the teenager had posted a picture of his grandfather's gun and that the weapon had a permit, Anutin said.
In addition to studying at school in the week, the 14-year-old attended tutoring classes over the weekends and enjoyed playing shooting games at the end of the day until midnight, Dejrapee said.
"The student was described as quiet, not very sociable, and fairly good academically," he said.
Friday's rampage has renewed scrutiny of gun regulations in Thailand, Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation with roughly 15 firearms per 100 residents.
Anutin, who tightened gun laws when he was interior minister following a previous mass shooting, said he will propose a new law to restrict the carrying of firearms by the public.
"As much as possible, we have to create an atmosphere of safety," he said. — Reuters

articles.title: Heavy rains trigger flooding in parts of PH amid Habagat
articles.summary: Continuous heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) triggered flooding in several parts of the country on Saturday.

blocks.text: Continuous heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) triggered flooding in several parts of the country on Saturday.
Metro Manila

In a social media update by GMA News reporter Bernadette Reyes, floodwaters in parts of Barangay Roxas District, Quezon City reached chest-deep levels. Residents said a flood control project in the area remains unfinished.
As of 12:20 p.m., a section of N.S. Amoranto Avenue corner Don Jose Street in Quezon City was also reported flooded, with one vehicle seen struggling to navigate the waters.
Other Stories
A section of Roxas Boulevard near Padre Faura and Pedro Gil streets in Manila was flooded but remained passable to motorists.
CALABARZON

In Batangas City, at least 49 individuals were evacuated to a school amid flooding in Barangay Libjo, according to a Facebook post by Coast Guard Station Batangas. One evacuee was transported in a wheelchair.

In Lian, Batangas, at least 33 residents were evacuated from their homes in Sitio Apalaya, Barangay Balibago. Authorities said they were transferred to Balibago Elementary School, which served as a temporary evacuation center.
In Mabini, Batangas, emergency responders relocated seven residents of Barangay Anilao East to Anilao East Elementary School as heavy rains persisted.

To assist stranded commuters in Batangas City, the Coast Guard District Southern Tagalog launched a Libreng Sakay (free ride) initiative, safely transporting at least 41 passengers to their destinations.
In a video captured by YouScooper Kimberly Falcon, a road in Kumintang Ilaya, Batangas City, was submerged in knee-deep floodwaters at around 10 a.m. following continuous heavy rain in the area.
Video footage captured by YouScooper Arn Ursais showed waist-deep flooding in parts of Medicion II-F, Imus, at around 7:30 a.m.
The state weather bureau PAGASA had raised an Orange Rainfall Warning over Imus, Cavite, as of 11 a.m.

In Kawit, Cavite, several families were evacuated from Barangay Gahak past midnight as floodwaters neared waist level. According to the Kawit MDRRMO Emergency Response Team, a total of 22 families were rescued, including senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and children.

In a social media update, GMA News reporter Jamie Santos said floodwaters in parts of Barangay Gahak had reached chest-deep levels. She noted that, according to residents, it was the first time they had experienced flooding this severe.

“Ayon po sa ilang mga residenteng nakausap po natin dito at ilang barangay official, bagaman itong lugar ay bahain naman po dati pa, ngayon lang daw po nila naranasan ‘yung ganitong kataas na pagbaha,” Santos said.
(According to some residents and barangay officials we spoke with, although this area has always been flood-prone, they said this is the first time they have experienced flooding at this height.)
“Hinala po nila, ito po ay dahil sa ilang estrukturang nakabara sa daluyan [ng] tubig malapit po sa ilog at ilang bahay na naitayo po doon,” she added.
(They suspect this is due to structures blocking the waterways near the river, as well as several houses built in the area.)

In Bacoor, Cavite, the local government unit reported road flooding as of Saturday afternoon. Officials also observed rising water levels along the Zapote River and at several other bridges across the city.
MIMAROPA
Residents in several low-lying and flood-prone areas across Romblon fled their homes as floodwaters continued to rise in their communities.

At around 1 a.m., at least 12 residents from three families were evacuated from Barangay Tulay, Odiongan. They were relocated to the Tulay Barangay Hall and the Municipal Evacuation Center in Barangay Dapawan, Odiongan.

In Sitio Maligaya Riverside, Barangay Poblacion, Looc, Romblon, at least 11 individuals were evacuated at around 2:05 a.m. Authorities said they were transferred to the barangay hall, which served as an emergency shelter.
A family of five in Barangay Madalag, Alcantara, was also evacuated by local authorities and brought to the barangay hall.

In Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro, YouScooper Hanna Mhae Famini captured knee-deep flooding in Barangay San Isidro at around 11 a.m. While rain continued in the area, floodwaters were slowly receding as of 4 p.m., she said.
Central Luzon
In Barangay Catangjalan, Obando, Bulacan, parts of the community were flooded as of noon. Roads remained passable to vehicles, with floodwaters reaching at least ankle-deep.

A pickup truck in Santa Maria, Bulacan, was forced to stop at Macaiban Bridge past 4 p.m. due to flooding. According to YouScooper Greddy Gabriel Bulatao, the driver immediately retreated after seeing the surging waters.
Local residents near the river said water had been overflowing onto the bridge since 1 p.m. following a day of continuous rain.
Ilocos Region

Several major roads in Dagupan City, including areas in the downtown district, were inundated following persistent rain showers. Residents faced difficult conditions while traversing flooded streets in the market area at around 6 a.m.
CAR
In a “24 Oras Weekend” report by Marisol Abdurahman on Saturday, a pine tree snapped from a slope and fell onto a road in Barangay Happy Hollow, Baguio City, at around 10 a.m.
Authorities cut the tree trunk into smaller pieces to clear the road and facilitate its removal.
Residents who witnessed the incident said they heard the tree crack before it fell onto the road.
“Biglang tumunog yung kahoy. Takbuhan kami kanina—dalawa kami. Sobrang nerbiyos, nanginginig,” recalled a resident who narrowly escaped being hit by the falling pine tree.
(The tree suddenly made a loud noise. The two of us immediately ran. We were extremely frightened and shaking.)
“Nung nakita nga po namin yung pagbagsak ng kahoy, yung dalawang tao buti na lang nakatakbo po sila… hindi inabot,” another resident added.
(When we saw the tree fall, thankfully, those two people managed to run out of the way in time.)
Another resident said a passing vehicle also narrowly escaped being crushed by the tree.
“May crack ka na pong maririnig tapos dahan-dahan na po siyang [tumumba], ma’am. May dumaan po na sasakyan, buti na lang po mas mabilis siya,” the resident said.
(You could hear a cracking sound before it slowly started to fall. A vehicle was passing by, but luckily, it was moving fast enough to get out of the way.)
According to the Baguio City Environment and Parks Management Office, the tree had already been leaning before the heavy rains.
"Hindi maiiwasan ngayong malakas po 'yung ulan, 'yung bagyo po. Nag-loosen 'yung soil kaya, ayun, ‘yun ‘yong isang cause,” said Junelyn Velasco, a Forester I from the city office.
(With the heavy rains and the tropical cyclone, this kind of incident is difficult to avoid. The soil loosened, which was one of the causes.) —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman to mayors: Check LGU offices for corruption in waste management contracts
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday called on mayors to scrutinize offices under their supervision for possible corruption in local garbage collection and waste management contracts.

blocks.text: Published August 8, 2026 4:45pm Updated August 8, 2026 6:54pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday called on mayors to scrutinize offices under their supervision for possible corruption in local garbage collection and waste management contracts.
In his radio program, Remulla commended some mayors, including Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte and Pasig City Mayor Vico Sotto, who refuse to be involved in such schemes.
However, Remulla pointed out that certain offices under their leadership may have been involved in corruption.

"Siguro sa Metro Manila, we can say Vico at Joy Belmonte. May mga iba pa, na hindi nila kailangan iyon. Hindi sila pumapatol. Sa ilalim nila—, 'yung mga opisina, Business Processing Licensing Office, Office of the Building Official. Lahat 'yan tsekin niyo," Remulla said.
Other Stories

(Maybe in Metro Manila, we can say Vico and Joy Belmonte. There are others who do not need that. They don't engage. Mayors, you should check the local Business Processing Licensing Office, Office of the Building Official, all the offices under you.)
"You should be aware of people under you who are committing shenanigans," he added.
In a statement, Belmonte said allegations of corruption should be investigated but warned against making sweeping accusations.

“It’s good that he made the clarification and offered good advice. As we said in our earlier statement at M4GG [Mayors for Good Governance], we share the belief that allegations of wrongdoing must be investigated, but sweeping accusations are dangerous because they undermine the integrity of many LCEs who are doing their best to practice good governance,” Belmonte said.

“In QC, we pursued digital transformation precisely to stop the culture of corruption and padulas. With our digital systems in place, mas madali na rin ma-trace kung sakaling merong kalokohan na ginagawa at the level of offices, kasi lahat ng transactions merong tracking numbers and digital footprint. Complementing the systems are our reforms for accountability. Rest assured na hindi tayo takot panagutin ang mga erring employees and officials kung mapatunayang lumabag at nagkamali,” she added.

(In QC, we pursued digital transformation precisely to stop the culture of corruption and padulas. With our digital systems in place, it is also easier to trace if there is any wrongdoing at the office level, because all transactions have tracking numbers and a digital footprint. Complementing the systems are our reforms for accountability. Rest assured that we are not afraid to hold erring employees and officials accountable if they are proven to have violated rules or committed wrongdoing.)
Meanwhile, Remulla called on the public to report irregularities involving mayors and offices under them.

"Ito ang challenge ko sa kanila, at saka sa taongbayan. Kung may reklamo kayo sa mayor, o sa nangyayari sa bayan na nag-apply kayo ng lisensiya. Ireklamo niyo sa mayor, furnish us a copy. Tapos, i-furnish-an niyo rin ng copy ang ARTA para magkaalaman kung sino ang kikilos sa atin," Remulla said, referring to the Anti-Red Tape Authority.

(This is my challenge to them, and also to the public. If you have a complaint against the mayor, or about what is happening in the area where you applied for a license. Complain to the mayor, furnish us with a copy. Then, furnish ARTA with a copy so that we know who will act.)
"'Pag ayaw kayong bigyan ng business permit, sabihin niyo," he added.
(If you are not given a business permit, tell us.) — VDV/VBL, GMA News
